audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not reflect the post-acquisition capital structure
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor omits Ultra PCS and Boyd earnings and the recurring interest, taxes, integration cash costs and other financing effects created by their acquisition.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, on January 23, 2026, the Company paid $1.53 billion, net of cash acquired, to acquire Ultra PCS Limited and the Company expects to close the acquisition of Boyd Thermal in the second quarter of 2026 for $9.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. Ultra PCS and Boyd closed in 2026 for $1,529 million and $9,549 million, while June debt reached $20,611 million. First-half net interest expense increased by $204 million year over year, but the acquired businesses also contributed $152 million of partial-period segment operating profit. Because the omitted benefits and costs run in opposite directions and affect the capitalized OE stream, the net valuation effect cannot be established from the supplied figures.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized post-close OE using trailing results and run-rate contributions from both acquisitions, including recurring financing interest, cash taxes, integration costs, purchase-accounting effects and the June 2026 balance sheet; then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The Mobility separation's economic leakage is absent from the continuing-value model
audit_findings.mechanism: The transaction changes the operating perimeter, Eaton and SpinCo/Dana share counts, ownership claims and equity bridge through the exchange offer, the approximately $1.1 billion cash distribution, allocated liabilities and transaction leakage.
audit_findings.evidence: Whether or not the spin-off is completed, our business may face material challenges in connection with this transaction, including, without limitation: the diversion of management’s attention from ongoing business concerns; attracting and retaining key management and other employees; retaining existing, or attracting new, business and operational relationships; foreseen and unforeseen dis-synergy costs, costs of restructuring transactions (including taxes) and other significant costs and expenses; and potential negative reactions from the financial markets if we fail to complete the spin-off as currently expected, within the anticipated time frame or at all.
audit_findings.explanation: The model capitalizes consolidated OE indefinitely even though definitive RMT agreements now provide for Mobility's separation. Mobility produced $405 million of 2025 segment operating profit and $198 million in the first half of 2026, while Eaton holders are expected to own at least 50.1% of the combined company and Eaton expects approximately $1.1 billion of cash before adjustments, taxes and charges. These are material components, but their net effect is unresolved because exchange terms, resulting share cancellation, liability allocation, stranded costs and the value of the distributed claim are not supplied.
audit_findings.action: When the Form 10 and exchange materials provide sufficient terms, value post-transaction Eaton and the SpinCo/Dana claim separately; incorporate the exchange ratio, resulting share counts, debt and cash allocation, stranded costs, separation spending, taxes and the final cash distribution.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims are missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,518 million gross, equal to $3.89 per share and 2.4% of the $63,399 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement cash not already captured in forecast taxes would require a bridge deduction or a reduction to future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the gross unrecognized income tax benefits totaled $1,300 million and interest and penalties were $218 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed $1,300 million of gross unrecognized tax benefits plus $218 million of interest and penalties is a real unresolved claim, although it is not a probability-weighted settlement amount. Even deducting the entire disclosed gross amount would reduce base value from $162.33 to about $158.44 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $390.85 market price. A larger unreserved loss is outside the quantified finding.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 tax reserve and its balance-sheet classification, estimate settlement amount and timing by dispute, and confirm that any bridge adjustment excludes amounts already reflected in forecast tax expense or OE.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension obligations may not be captured by accounting earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $497 million, equal to $1.27 per share and 0.8% of the $63,399 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The deficit would reduce the equity bridge or OE to the extent required cash contributions exceed pension expense already reflected in earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the net unfunded position of $497 million in pension liabilities consisted of $587 million in plans that have no funding requirements and $166 million in plans that require funding, offset by $256 million in plans that are overfunded.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE calculation already captures contributions remains unresolved, but the filed deficit provides a conservative scale test. Deducting the entire $497 million would reduce base value from $162.33 to about $161.06 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. The June 2026 remeasurement improved funded status by $47 million, so the December figure does not understate the direction of the disclosed interim movement.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded-status calculation at the valuation date and reconcile actual and projected employer contributions against pension expense in OE; adjust only for the portion not already captured.

audit_findings.title: The associate-stake addition appears to use carrying value as equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Replacing the $903 million bridge addition with realizable after-tax fair value would directly increase or decrease equity value; any unpurged associate income would also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Investments in associate companies included in Other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheets were $ 903 million and $ 872 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact match demonstrates that carrying value was used, but the record supplies no independent fair value or disposal leakage. The recorded addition itself equals $2.31 per share, or 1.4% of base equity value, so eliminating it entirely would not change the conclusion. Material upside or a different downside cannot be established without values for the underlying associates, making this an unresolved valuation possibility rather than a demonstrated material error.
audit_findings.action: Identify each associate and latest ownership percentage, obtain an independently supportable fair value and estimated disposal taxes or restrictions, verify that all $8 million of 2025 associate income was purged, and rerun the bridge if the supported net value differs materially from $903 million.

audit_findings.title: A synthetic-lease residual guarantee is outside the recognized lease bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $157.25 million, equal to $0.40 per share and 0.25% of the $63,399 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Upon commencement, lease payments enter OE and a lease liability or probability-weighted residual shortfall may affect the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The lease arrangement contains a residual value guarantee of approximately 85 % of the total construction cost.
audit_findings.explanation: The facility was still expected to commence in the first half of 2027, so this is principally a forward-looking item not yet present in the supplied June balance sheet. The stated guarantee is 85% of approximately $185 million of construction cost; even treating that full amount as a loss would not change the current valuation conclusion. Actual exposure should be lower to the extent the facility retains residual value, but future rent and final construction economics are not supplied.
audit_findings.action: At lease commencement, verify classification, recognized liability, final construction cost, rental commitments and guaranteed residual value; include lease cash costs in OE and separately recognize only residual exposure not already captured.
